entities.summary:
The Kosovo War was a late 1990s armed conflict in Kosovo that took place from 1998 to 1999. The conflict began on February 1, 1998, and ended on June 11, 1999. The war was fought between the Yugoslav government, led by Slobodan Milošević, and the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), a separatist group seeking independence for Kosovo. The conflict resulted in the deaths of over 13,000 people, the displacement of hundreds of thousands, and the intervention of NATO forces.

The war had significant consequences for the region and the world. The conflict led to the establishment of UN administration in Kosovo, which remained in place until 2008. The war also had a profound impact on the people of Kosovo, who suffered greatly during the conflict. The war also had a significant impact on the politics of the region, leading to the ousting of Slobodan Milošević from power.

The legacy of the Kosovo War can be seen in the continued tensions between Kosovo and Serbia, as well as the ongoing efforts to rebuild and recover from the conflict.

The Kosovo War serves as a reminder of the importance of diplomacy and international intervention in preventing and ending conflicts. Despite the challenges and difficulties of the conflict, the international community came together to support the people of Kosovo and bring an end to the fighting.
